topic: Complete state-specific identification under observed-context CSIs. In finite positive semi-Markovian DAGs, require every CSI activation variable to be observed and substitute the fixed treatment/outcome assignments before partitioning contexts. Construct a terminating sound-and-complete procedure returning either an arithmetic observed-cell formula for P_x(y), or a verified observed LC-certificate: an activation-refining partition, CSI-authorized deletion traces, SUCCESS ID-Qfunc derivations or OBSTRUCTION rooted C-forest pairs for every relevant c-component, and two global positive algebraic CPT tables indexed by the input CSI row-equality quotient that induce the same P(V) but different queries. Prove global shared-row gluing, total formula recovery or a genuine forest obstruction, and finite complexity; generic real-algebraic decision without the context/C-forest characterization does not count. Use Chen-Darwiche 2026, Tikka et al. 2019, and Mokhtarian et al. 2022 as anchors, and Y0 as the software consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The observed-context restriction removes an exact hidden-activation obstruction. Global CSI CPT rows reduce to connected equality classes, and fixed-nuisance binary-sink countermodels reduce exactly to a rational row-space/nullspace test. Two positive rational examples were checked, with query gaps 1/30 and 3/200. Active pruning, shared-row identification, cancellation, positive denominators, fixed cardinalities, and empty-trace decoration were attacked; saturated local-forest reasoning fails, but the literal partial-trace/global-witness certificate survives. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the finite global context-factor dichotomy: exhaustive sound reductions must yield a total arithmetic formula or partial-trace rooted-forest obstructions admitting jointly positive shared-row countermodels, without the forests becoming merely decorative generic algebraic witnesses. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the five-node active-deletion example where the pruned graph has no hedge but the empty trace has one, then test a local bow whose target becomes identified through an observed reference context; failure to reject the false local countermodel, or inability to link the surviving forest to query separation, forces a pivot or stop. open_problems.why_unsolved: The ordinary hedge construction chooses local kernels independently, whereas CSI equates CPT rows across activation contexts. The prior CausalSmith proof explicitly lacks a joint inverse lift for overlapping ancestor paths and shows that a positive local contrast can disappear after global contraction. Thus a locally valid forest pair may violate the row quotient or cancel after marginalization. Generic polynomial separation can verify a model pair but does not prove that the recorded forest is the load-bearing obstruction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if obstruction theorem and constructive compiler producing two strictly positive rational quotient-indexed CPT tables, with proofs of shared-row compatibility, equality of P(V), a nonzero P_x(y) gap, and an auditable partial-trace C-forest lineage.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing pruning results preserve a query in one ordinary graph. A CSI deletion is state-dependent: the five-node failure pattern can erase a hedge from the active pruned graph even though the empty trace retains one, while a local bow can be identified through a reference context sharing its CPT rows. The prior executable theorem omits its initial selected-separation failure branch, so neither safe formula recovery nor lifting of an earlier obstruction has been established.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient trace-pruning theorem with explicit maps recovering formulas from safe branches and lifting every retained rooted C-forest to the original shared-row model, including a verified treatment of the initial-failure branch.

The missing step is a quotient-aware characterization relating the local perturbation space, context-factor recombination, and the exact fixed-cell query functional.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Chen and Darwiche show that fixed x,y cells require a finer identification theory, while Tikka et al. provide sound search but not a complete characterization. Mokhtarian et al.'s completeness reduction depends on root controls, where intervention and conditioning on a control context coincide in the required way; that step fails when an observed activation has parents. Substituting x,y first can activate deletions and expose cancellations that variable-level ID and independent contextwise ID do not capture.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite algorithm proving that every input yields either an arithmetic functional of positive observed cells equal to P_x(y) or a verified nonidentification certificate, together with termination, soundness, completeness, and finite-complexity bounds.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The representation literature provides labels, stages, and equivalence results, but complete interventional results concern restricted fully observed models rather than latent semi-Markovian observational fibers. Overlapping CSI statements create transitive equalities between CPT rows in graphically distinct contexts. The prior CausalSmith work shows that local contrasts can cancel globally and lacks a joint inverse lift, so decomposing contexts before forming the equality quotient may both invent false countermodels and lose valid formulas.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A canonical row-quotient theorem proving invariance of fixed-cell identifiability, returned arithmetic formulas, and globally glued countermodel certificates when the input CSI list is replaced by its connected CPT-row equality quotient.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known hardness concerns general CSI input, whereas known tractability relies on observed root controls and enumeration of their assignments. With endogenous observed activations, that reduction fails, but fixed x,y substitution and equality-class quotienting may collapse exponentially many syntactic contexts. Existing results do not locate the boundary or show whether producing formulas and explicit certificates is fixed-parameter tractable in quotient or trace width.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a formula-or-certificate algorithm with running time f(k)poly(|G|,|CSI|) for a precisely defined context parameter k, or a matching parameterized hardness theorem under standard complexity assumptions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its complexity discussion cleanly contrasts general CSI hardness with enumeration over a fixed set of root controls.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: General CSI identification is intractable -> root-control structure restores contextwise tractability -> endogenous observed activations require a new parameterized boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the paper's nonidentifiability hardness reduction while preserving observed activation and fixed-state restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It establishes the baseline lower bound that a proposed parameterized regime must evade.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate control contexts, reduce each to polynomial-time Q-function identification, and bound total work by the control-domain size.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the natural upper-bound template to generalize from root controls to quotient-refined activation traces.

literature_map:
1. Boutilier, Friedman, Goldszmidt, and Koller (UAI 1996) introduced CSI as assignment-specific regularity in local conditional tables.
2. Pensar, Nyman, Koski, and Corander (DMKD 2015, arXiv:1310.1187) encode CSI through LDAG edge labels and study observational equivalence.
3. Shpitser and Pearl (AAAI 2006) give ordinary semi-Markovian ID its formula-or-hedge completeness architecture using Q-factors and rooted C-forests.
4. Huang and Valtorta (AAAI 2006, arXiv:1206.6831) independently connect complete identification algorithms with completeness of do-calculus.
5. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:2009.09768) prove general CSI nonidentifiability NP-hard and give a terminating sound calculus and search.
6. Their crucial negative result is that identification in every context-specific DAG does not imply global CSI identification.
7. Mokhtarian, Jamshidi, Etesami, and Kiyavash (AISTATS 2022, arXiv:2110.12064) obtain completeness only for observed root controls by reducing each control assignment to ordinary identification.
8. Their fixed-control tractability result contrasts with general CSI hardness and isolates the missing endogenous-activation regime.
9. Chen and Darwiche (2025, arXiv:2412.02869) cast CSI as parameter constraints and use arithmetic circuits for constrained identification, without a forest-grounded complete characterization.
10. Chen and Darwiche (UAI 2026, arXiv:2510.16703) show that state-specific effects may be identifiable when variable-based effects are not.
11. Duarte and Solus (JRSSB 2026, arXiv:2101.09271) give positive factorization and equivalence theory for fully observed CStrees, clarifying shared-row semantics.
12. Tikka and Karvanen (JMLR 2018, arXiv:1806.07085) and Chen and Barker (ICLR 2026) study query-preserving pruning separately from CSI witness lifting.
13. Kivva, Etesami, and Kiyavash (UAI 2023, arXiv:2306.11755) supply positivity-aware identification and countermodel constructions.
14. Duarte et al. (JASA 2024, arXiv:2109.13471) reduce finite causal questions to polynomial programs, validating algebraic witnesses without tying them to CSI forests.
15. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (JMLR 2022, arXiv:2003.12659) connect hidden-variable identification to influence-function and weight-based estimation.
